transcript:
00:00 Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we, uh, scheduled an hour, we've got a couple extra minutes if needed. quick intros please.
00:08 Dr. Priya Shah (Customer): Hi I'm Priya, head of data at Acme Healthcare. we're looking to validate quality for clinical summarization and a triage chat assistant.
00:15 Marco (Customer): Marco, ML Eng, i'll be owning data and the sample set.
00:20 Jordan (AE): Great. Samir, you want to intro?
00:23 Samir (SE): Yeah, Samir Patel, solutions engineer on Redwood, I'll run the benchmarks and help with evals, thanks.
00:30 Jordan (AE): High-level goal for this POC is to prove model choice and serving profile can meet your accuracy and hallucination targets while hitting cost targets. we proposed a 4-week POC: week 0 setup, week 1 bench, weeks 2-3 regression/eval, week 4 demo + decision. does that align?
00:45 Dr. Priya Shah: Sounds reasonable. our main success criteria: less than 8% hallucination on clinical facts, BLEU/ROUGE-type or clinical F1 above baseline from our current fine-tuned model, and turnaround latency under 1 second for single-turn triage responses in 95th percentile. cost target is about $0.0006 per token-equivalent, roughly.
01:05 Samir (SE): couple quick clarifications — when you say hallucination threshold, do you have an existing eval set with ground truth or do we need to create golden annotations?
01:14 Dr. Priya Shah: we have a small curated golden set of ~300 clinical summaries and about 200 chat logs with verified labels. we can expand if needed.
01:24 Jordan (AE): Perfect, that maps to our suggestion: golden prompts + golden outputs for regression testing. we'll run a baseline model set (open models + our recommended quantized variants) and compare.
01:33 Marco: For workload sizing, you're saying 300/200, but we also have a backlog of 20k notes, will that matter?
01:39 Samir (SE): For benching we only need a representative sample. 500 documents and 200 chats is ideal — gives good distribution across lengths and edge cases. bulk migration isn't required for the POC.
01:51 Tina (Customer - Compliance): quick compliance question — do you support BYOK / KMS and can we run this in a VPC?
01:57 Jordan (AE): Yes, our Private and Dedicated options support customer-managed keys (KMS), HSM integrations in some cases, and VPC peering; we'll schedule a deeper security review after this call.
02:06 Marco: What about data retention and logs? we need audit logs for every token/route for compliance.
02:12 Samir (SE): We can capture request/response logs and provide token-level cost breakdowns. we'll scrub PHI per your guidance and can do retention policy config; but for the POC we usually keep minimal logs unless you request otherwise.
02:25 Jordan (AE): Ok. moving to benchmarks — primary metrics: latency p50/p95, throughput for batching, cost per token normalized, and quality metrics: accuracy, hallucination rate, format compliance (structured fields). We'll run stress tests at your target QPS to validate autoscaling.
02:40 Marco: what's a realistic throughput number? our triage may peak at 40 qps during mornings.
02:45 Samir (SE): Dedicated can sustain that with moderate batch sizes; we'll propose instance counts after we see seq length distribution, but 40 QPS is well within a Dedicated pool.
02:55 Jordan (AE): Now the heart — quality eval plan. Samir will own the eval harness but here's the proposed approach:
03:04 Samir (SE): Step 1: Golden prompts. we'll collect your curated golden prompts and outputs into a spreadsheet (shared). they become the canonical test set for regression. we'll enforce input normalization (strip PHI placeholders if required).
03:15 Samir (SE): Step 2: Regression tests. run the golden set across each model variant nightly or per-run; compute diffs vs gold using multiple metrics — token-level accuracy for extractive fields, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and custom clinical F1 for named entities.
03:30 Dr. Priya Shah: For clinical F1 we need entity-level scoring for medications, dosages, diagnoses. can you support that?
03:36 Samir (SE): Yes, we can plug in your entity extractor to compute span-level F1. if you don't want to expose PHI, you can provide anonymized annotations.
03:44 Jordan (AE): Step 3: Hallucination checks. we'll run factuality detectors plus an automated contradiction check vs the patient's notes and a human review for edge cases. note: automated detectors aren't perfect so we recommend a sampling of flagged outputs for human validation.
03:59 Marco: can we get model-level provenance? like exactly which checkpoint and quantization profile was used for each run?
04:04 Lee (SE): absolutely — each run is tagged with model version, quant level, kernels used, and hardware SKU. that gets logged in the run artifact and the console.
04:12 Tina: format checks — some of our outputs must be JSON with keys present; can we validate structure and required fields?
04:18 Samir (SE): yes, we'll include schema validation (JSON schema) as part of the pipeline; failures will be counted as regressions.
04:26 Jordan (AE): Scoring approach: composite score combining clinical F1 (weight 50%), hallucination rate (30%), format compliance (10%), and latency/cost penalties (10%). thresholds to pass will be agreed — e.g., composite >= 0.85, hallucination <= 8%.
04:45 Dr. Priya Shah: that weighting seems ok but we might weight hallucination higher; patient safety first. we'll propose adjustments in writing.
04:52 Jordan (AE): noted. on benchmarks, we recommend running 3 variants: baseline (your current fine-tuned), candidate open model (quantized), and a higher-capacity model to measure tradeoffs.
05:01 Marco: timeline — you said set up week 0, week 1 bench. how long is regression/eval?
05:06 Jordan (AE): typically 2 weeks for regression/eval for a POC of this size; that includes QA, analyst review of hallucinations, and a final results presentation. so total 4 weeks.
05:16 Samir (SE): For the 1-week benchmark we'll run synthetic load plus golden set runs. Bench config will include: batch sizes [1,4,8], seq lengths distribution (we'll request histograms), and quant profiles (int8, int4 where supported).
05:30 Marco: are there any gotchas with quantization and clinical accuracy?
05:34 Samir (SE): yes, quant can affect factuality for small models; that's why we'll compare variants and also run regression tests on golden prompts to measure any drop.
05:43 Dr. Priya Shah: about hallucination detection — you mentioned contradiction checks; can you explain?
05:48 Samir (SE): sure. we run the output through a verifier that checks for statements contradicted by the source notes (exact match, entity mismatch). also, we use a factuality model that scores claims; anything below threshold is flagged for human review. false positives exist so sampling is important.
06:03 Jordan (AE): ops questions — procurement, do you need an MSA or can we do an initial POC NDA + SOW?
06:10 Mark (Procurement): we'll likely want a short SOW and NDAs; MSA later if we proceed. give us pricing for a 4-week Dedicated bench plus optional Private onboarding.
06:19 Jordan (AE): we'll include a pricing matrix in the follow-up.
06:23 Tina: regarding logs, can logs be redacted before they leave our VPC?
06:28 Samir (SE): there's support for client-side redaction or agent-side redaction; we'll document options.
06:34 Speaker 1: (inaudible)
06:36 Jordan (AE): ok next steps recap — Jordan to share POC plan and golden prompt template, Samir to send benchmark config, Marco to upload samples, Tina to send compliance checklist, schedule security deep-dive next week. any objections?
06:48 Dr. Priya Shah: none.
06:50 Jordan (AE): great. before we finish a couple of small details: scoring thresholds, who signs off on pass/fail?
06:56 Dr. Priya Shah: Priya and Marco will be internal sign-offs; Redwood will present results.
07:02 Jordan (AE): perfect. we'll aim to start setup by Feb 18. thanks everyone.
07:07 Marco: thanks.
07:09 Jordan (AE): talk soon. bye.
